text: {"rules":[{"id":"PED-VISION-ACUITY-4-5","version":"2025","title":"Visual acuity screening at ages 4 and 5 years (Bright Futures/AAP periodicity schedule, footnote 7)","source_quote":"A visual acuity screen is recommended at ages 4 and 5 years, as well as in cooperative 3-year-olds.","grade":"not graded (AAP/Bright Futures consensus recommendation)","effective_date":"2025-02","action":"Perform a visual acuity screen for children aged 4 and 5 years.","denominator":"{\"age\": {\"min\": 4, \"max\": 5, \"at\": \"end\"}, \"quote\": \"at ages 4 and 5 years\"}","numerator":"{\"procedure\": {\"concept\": \"visual_acuity_screening\", \"window\": [\"{MY}-01-01\", \"{MY}-12-31\"]}, \"quote\": \"A visual acuity screen\", \"derived\": {\"window\": \"screen is due at the age-4 and age-5 visits; a child aged 4 or 5 at end of the measurement year reached that age during the year, so one acuity screen within the measurement year is expected\"}}","exclusions":"[]"}],"coverage_notes":["New concept 'visual_acuity_screening' used because the vocabulary's 'vision_screening' does not distinguish a visual acuity screen from instrument-based screening, which this footnote treats separately.","Vision footnote 7: 'as well as in cooperative 3-year-olds' needs a clinician judgment of cooperation and was not encoded; a separate rule would need {uncomputable: child cooperation}.","Vision footnote 7: instrument-based screening at 12 and 24 months and at 3 through 5 years is permissive ('may be used'), so no rule was made.","Periodicity grid: the extracted text loses column alignment. The 'l' and risk-assessment marks for each row (history, measurements, BMI, blood pressure, vision, hearing, maternal depression, developmental, autism, behavioral, tobacco/alcohol/drug, depression/suicide, physical exam, newborn blood/bilirubin/CCHD, immunization, anemia, lead, TB, dyslipidemia, STI, HIV, HBV, HCV, sudden cardiac arrest, cervical dysplasia, oral health, fluoride varnish/supplementation, anticipatory guidance) cannot be mapped reliably to ages, and no verbatim quote would contain the ages. No rules were made from the grid.","Risk-assessment items (the 'ê' marks: assess risk, act if positive) depend on clinician risk assessment and are uncomputable.","Hearing footnote 10 (audiometry including 6,000 and 8,000 Hz once between 11 and 14, 15 and 17, and 18 and 21 years) was not encoded. It needs birthdate-relative windows that measurement-year windows cannot express, and the vocabulary has no concept for high-frequency audiometry.","Hearing footnotes 8 and 9 (confirm newborn screen, verify results, follow up) depend on prior results and follow-up and were not encoded.","Footnote 1 catch-up logic (bring the schedule up to date at the earliest possible time) was not represented.","Footnote 2: a prenatal visit for high-risk or first-time parents, or on request, depends on uncomputable parent status and a request. Not encoded.","Footnotes 3 and 4: newborn evaluation after birth, within 3 to 5 days of birth, within 48 to 72 hours after discharge, and within 48 hours of discharge if discharged under 48 hours. These use birth- and discharge-relative timing that measurement-year windows cannot express, and breastfeeding support is not encodable.","Footnote 6: blood pressure measurement before age 3 only for infants and children with specific risk conditions. Risk conditions are unspecified, and screening otherwise follows an external guideline. Not encoded.","Footnotes 5, 11, 12 and 13 (BMI/obesity, maternal depression, developmental and autism screening) only refer to external guidelines and state no ages or intervals in this section. Not encoded.","Footnotes 14-38 are not in this section and were not represented."]}
